Rashi on Shabbat 117b:10:1.english: Holding two - He holds them in his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:10:2.hebrew: לקטו כתיב - דמשמע אחיזה, אבל בציעה לא כתיב משנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:10:2.english: “They collected” is written - Which implies holding [two loaves], but [regarding] breaking [them], “double” is not written.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:10:3.hebrew: בצע לכוליה שירותיה - פרוסה גדולה, ודי לו בה לאותה סעודה, ולכבוד שבת, ונראה כמחבב סעודת שבת להתחזק ולאכול הרבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:10:3.english: He would break [for] his entire meal - [He would break] a large slice, and it sufficed for him for that meal; and [he did so] in honor of Shabbat, and he appears as one who cherishes the Shabbat meal, to strengthen himself and eat a lot.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:10:4.english: When [it] happened [to come] to them - Sometimes the eiruv [was] in their house, and sometimes in the house of one of the other people.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:10:5.hebrew: שרו ביה - היינו ברכת המוציא, שהיא התחלת אכילה. שרו — מתחילין:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:10:5.english: They would begin with it - This refers to the Hamotzi blessing, which is the beginning of eating. [Sharu means] they begin.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:11:1.english: Three [mentions of] "today" - It comes for the count of three meals.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:1:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב אשי כו' - בין רבנן ובין בן בתירא כר' אליעזר סבירא להו, דבעי ג' מחיצות וב' לחיים בעלמא. והכא לגבי ספר, אמרי רבנן מודה ר' אליעזר בלחי אחד, ובן בתירא אמר דמודה ר' אליעזר אף בלא לחי:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:1:1.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said, etc. - Both the Rabbis and Ben Beteira hold in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who requires three walls and two posts in general. And here, regarding a [Torah] scroll, the Rabbis say [that] Rabbi Eliezer concedes [that it is permitted] with one post, and Ben Beteira says that Rabbi Eliezer concedes [that it is permitted] even without a post.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:1:2.english: One post is sufficient for it - They are explaining the statement of the Rabbis.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:2:1.english: [If] a fire broke out on the night of Shabbat - before eating.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:2:3.hebrew: לעולם הוא מציל - הואיל ויומא בר הכי הוא, ובהיתרא טרח — דהא בני טלטול נינהו ולחצר המעורבת — ואפי' טובא הוה שרי ליה אי לאו משום גזירה, וכדמפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:2:3.english: He may always rescue - Since the day is fit for this, and he is exerting himself in a permitted manner — for they [the food items] are fit for carrying, and [he is carrying them] into a courtyard joined by an eruv — even a great deal would be permitted to him, were it not for a [rabbinic] decree, and as it explains in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:1.english: Now, since he is exerting himself in a permitted [manner] - [They] are fit for carrying, and [he is taking them] to a courtyard with an eruv.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:2.hebrew: ואי שרית ליה - לאתחולי בהצלה כולי האי, מתוך שהוא בהול, מינשי ליה שבת ואתי נמי לכבויי:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:2.english: And if you permit him - to begin rescuing so much, since he is agitated, he will forget [that it is] Shabbat and will also come to extinguish [the fire].

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:3.english: And catch - a stream falling from the air.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:4.hebrew: ויצרף - סמוך לגג, כעין שאיבה, אלא שאינו ראוי לשאוב, שהגג חלק והיין אינו בגומא. מצרף כלי לגג שיזוב מן הגג לכלי, והוא אוחז הכלי בידו:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:4.english: And attach - [Holding it] close to the roof, similar to drawing [liquid], except that it is not fit for drawing, since the roof is smooth and the wine is not in a hollow. [Instead,] he attaches a vessel to the roof so that [the wine] will flow from the roof into the vessel, while he holds the vessel in his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:5.hebrew: התם מאי גזירה איכא - כיון דמידי דהתירא הוא, אמאי לא יקלוט ויצרף:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:5.english: There, what decree is there - Since it is a permitted matter, why may he not catch [the liquid] and attach [another vessel]?

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:6.hebrew: שמא יביא כלי כו' - מתוך שהוא מחזר על כלים הרבה, ישכח ויביא:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:3:6.english: Lest he bring a vessel, etc. - Since he goes around looking for many vessels, he will forget and bring [one through the public domain].

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:4:1.hebrew: ולא יקלוט ואח"כ יזמין - אורחים, דבשעת קליטה לא מיבעיא ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:4:1.english: And one may not catch [the liquid] and afterward invite - guests, for at the time of catching he does not need [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:4:2.english: One may not employ artifice in this - [That is,] to invite guests who do not need to eat, so that they will leave [it] over.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:5:1.hebrew: שנפלו לבור - בי"ט, ואין שניהם ראוים לשחיטה ביום אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:5:1.english: That fell into a pit - On a Festival, and both of them are not fit for slaughter on one day.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:5:2.english: And [he] does not slaughter it - For he finds a pretext, [saying,] "Perhaps the other one is fatter than it."

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:6:1.hebrew: עד כאן לא קאמר ר' אליעזר - דאין מערימין:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:6:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer only stated - that one may not employ artifice.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:7:1.english: [If] one rescued fine bread - [Enough] for three meals.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:7:2.hebrew: לא יציל פת הדראה - פת קיבר שניטל הדרה, לפי שאין ערמה כשרה לומר פת הדראה נוחה לי:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:7:2.english: He may not rescue coarse bread - [This is] coarse bread whose splendor has been removed, [and he may not rescue it] because it is not a valid artifice to say, "Coarse bread is more agreeable to me."

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:7:3.hebrew: אבל לא משבת ליום הכפורים - כגון אם חל יוה"כ באחד בשבת, דהא לא אכיל עד לאורתא, ולאורתא ליטרח ולייתי:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:7:3.english: However, not from Shabbat for Yom Kippur - For example, if Yom Kippur falls on Sunday, for he does not eat until the evening, and in the evening let him exert himself and bring [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:7:4.hebrew: ואין צריך לומר משבת לי"ט - דיכול להכין בו ביום:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:7:4.english: And needless to say, on Shabbat for a Festival - For one can prepare [food] on that day.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:8:1.hebrew: מרדה - כלי שרודין בו הפת ומפרידין אותו מכותל התנור שנדבק בה. לא ירדה אותו במרדה, שהוא דרך חול:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:8:1.english: A baker's paddle - A utensil with which one removes bread and separates it from the wall of the oven to which it adhered. He should not remove it with a baker's paddle, for that is the weekday manner.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:9:1.hebrew: ישכים אדם - בע"ש לטרוח ולזמן הוצאת שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:9:1.english: A person should rise early - On the eve of Shabbat [Friday], to exert oneself and prepare the expenditures for Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:9:2.hebrew: והכינו את אשר יביאו לאלתר - בשעת הבאה הכנה, והבאה בהשכמה היא, דכתיב וילקטו אותו בבקר בבקר (שמות ט״ז:כ״א):
Rashi on Shabbat 117b:9:2.english: And they shall prepare that which they bring — immediately - At the time of bringing [the manna is] the preparation, and the bringing is early in the morning, as it is written, "And they gathered it morning by morning" (Exodus 16:21).

Rashi on Shabbat 117b:9:3.english: To break [bread] - [When reciting] the blessing of Hamotzi.

Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:3:1.hebrew: הא דתניא נשברה לו חבית בראש גגו - הקשה הרב פורת: אמאי לא פריך ממתניתין דריש חבית (לקמן שבת קמג:), דתנן: "חבית שנשברה, מצילין ממנה מזון שלש סעודות, ואומר לאחרים בואו והצילו לכם, ובלבד שלא יספוג"? ותירץ, דההיא איכא למימר כגון שהחבית בכרמלית, דחיישינן שמא יעביר כלי ד' אמות בכרמלית; אבל בהך ברייתא קתני בהדיא "בראש גגו". ור"י תירץ, דהתם מיירי כשנשפך היין לארץ, דחיישינן שמא יספוג. אומר ה"ר שמואל בשם ר"ת, דדוקא נשברה לו חבית, אבל נסדקה ועושה טיף טיף — מותר להביא כלים לקלוט ולצרף, דאינו בהול כל כך להביא כלים דרך רה"ר כמו כשנשברה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:3:1.english: That which was taught [in a baraita]: "If one's barrel broke atop his roof." - Rabbi Porat asked: Why did [Abaye] not challenge [Rava] from our Mishnah at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Chavit (later, Shabbat 143b), where we learned: "If a barrel broke, one may rescue from it food for three meals, and he may say to others, 'Come and rescue for yourselves,' provided that he does not sponge [it up]"? And he answered that in that case [of the Mishnah], one can say [it refers to a case] such as where the barrel is in a karmelit, where we are concerned lest he carry a vessel four cubits in a karmelit; whereas in this baraita it explicitly teaches "atop his roof." And Rabbeinu Yitzchak answered that there [in the Mishnah] it is speaking of a case where the wine spilled onto the ground, where we are concerned lest he sponge [it up]. Rabbi Shmuel says in the name of Rabbeinu Tam that specifically [when] his barrel broke [is it prohibited to catch or attach another vessel]; however, [if] it cracked and is dripping drop by drop, it is permitted to bring vessels to catch [the wine] and to attach [another vessel], because he is not so agitated as to bring vessels through the public domain as [he is] when it broke.

Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:3:2.hebrew: כלי אחר ויקלוט, כלי אחר ויצרף - אומר ר"י דזו אף זו קתני: לא מבעי לקלוט, דמינכר שמציל, דאסור; אלא אפילו לצרף, דלא מינכר כולי האי שהוא מציל, אסור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:3:2.english: "Another vessel to catch [the liquid], another vessel to attach" - Ri says that [the baraita] teaches [in the style of] "this, and even that": needless to say that catching [the liquid], where it is noticeable that he is rescuing [it], is forbidden, but even attaching [another vessel], where it is not so noticeable that he is rescuing [it], is forbidden.

Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:7:1.hebrew: הציל פת נקיה לא יציל פת הדראה - אומר ר"י: כשאפו בי"ט של פסח מצות מסולת נקיה, שיש לו די לצורך י"ט, אין אופין אחריהן פת של הדראה; אלא מתחילה יעשה של הדראה, ואחרי כן יעשה הנקיה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:7:1.english: "If one rescued fine bread, he may not rescue coarse bread [hadra'a]" - Rabbi Yitzchak says: When they bake matzot from fine flour on the Festival of Passover, [such] that he has enough for the needs of the Festival, they may not bake coarse bread after them; rather, first he should make [bread] of coarse [flour], and afterward he should make the fine [bread].

Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:7:2.hebrew: אבל לא משבת ליום הכפורים - פירש בקונטרס למוצאי יוה"כ. וא"ת: פשיטא, דחול גמור הוא, ומ"ש משבת למוצאי שבת? וי"ל: דמצוה לאכול במוצאי יוה"כ, כדפי' לעיל (שבת דף קיד:); ועוד, לפי שהתענו — מותר יותר. אי נמי: ליום הכפורים עצמו קאמר, ולהאכיל התינוקות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:7:2.english: However, not on Shabbat for Yom Kippur - Rashi explained [that this refers] to the conclusion of Yom Kippur. And if you ask: [Isn't] it obvious, for it is a completely ordinary weekday, and how does it differ from [rescuing on] Shabbat for the conclusion of Shabbat? One can answer: Because it is a mitzvah to eat at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, as explained above (Shabbat 114b); and furthermore, [one might think that] because they fasted, it is more permitted. Alternatively, [the Baraita] is speaking of Yom Kippur itself, and [refers to rescuing food] to feed the young children.

Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:8:1.hebrew: והתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל כל מלאכת עבודה לא תעשו - וא"ת: ואמאי מייתי קרא ד"כל מלאכת עבודה" דכתיב גבי י"ט? הא אפי' בשבת — דכתיב "לא תעשה מלאכה" סתם, ולא כתיב "עבודה" — שרי לתקוע ולרדות מן התורה, כדמשמע הכא דאשבת מייתי לה! ופירש רבינו שמואל דגרס: "כל מלאכה לא תעשו". ורשב"א מפרש דלעולם מ"כל מלאכת עבודה" אימעיט תקיעה ורדייה, ושבת ילפינן מי"ט, דאין בין י"ט לשבת אלא אוכל נפש בלבד, כדכתיב: "אך אשר יאכל לכל נפש" (שמות י״ב:ט״ז):
Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:8:1.english: And did not the school of Rabbi Yishmael teach: "You shall not do any laborious work" - And if you will ask: Why does [the Gemara] cite the verse of "any laborious work," which is written concerning a Festival [Yom Tov]? Even on Shabbat — where it is written "you shall not do work" unqualified, and "laborious" is not written — it is permitted by Torah law to blow [the shofar] and to remove [bread from the oven], as is implied here, since [the Gemara] cites it regarding Shabbat! Rabbeinu Shmuel explained that he reads the text as: "You shall not do any work." And Rashba explains that in fact, blowing [the shofar] and removing [bread] are excluded from "any laborious work," and we derive Shabbat from Yom Tov, for there is no difference between Yom Tov and Shabbat except [regarding] food preparation alone, as it is written: "only that which may be eaten by every person" (Exodus 12:16).

Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:8:2.hebrew: שהיא חכמה ואינה מלאכה - וכיון דמדאורייתא שריא, אע"ג דמדרבנן אסירא — כדאמר בראש השנה (דף לג.): "אין מעכבין את התינוקות מלתקוע, הא נשים מעכבין" — הכא הוה לן למישרי משום ג' סעודות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 117b:8:2.english: Which is a skill and not a labor - And since by Torah law it is permitted — even though by rabbinic law it is forbidden, as it says in Rosh Hashanah (33a): "We do not prevent children from blowing [the shofar]," [implying] that women we do prevent — here [in the case of removing bread from the oven] we should have permitted [removing it in the usual manner] because of [the mitzvah of] three meals.
